sections.body: The AI Economist covers ten areas where artificial intelligence is changing how economies are measured and how capital is allocated. In forecasting, models now mix traditional econometrics with high frequency data, central bank text, and nowcasting to estimate growth and inflation between official releases. Quantitative trading uses machine learning to search prices, order books, and news for signals, then execute trades with varying levels of automation. Private equity and credit teams use AI to screen companies, parse merger and acquisition filings, score borrowers, and monitor covenants. Portfolio construction applies optimization and reinforcement learning to asset weights, while market language work turns earnings calls, filings, and news into sentiment and topic measures. Alternative data, from satellite images to card transactions, feeds many of these tasks, and agent workflows chain models together for research, reconciliation, and reporting, while crypto markets and decentralised finance add a 24 hour programmatic setting for market making, risk monitoring, and fraud detection, all under governance and fiduciary risk that sets the rules, disclosures, and duties.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are mature: data cleaning, backtesting infrastructure, anomaly detection, and text extraction from filings are routine. Forecasting remains hard because economies are non stationary and structural breaks defeat historical patterns. Trading models often decay, overfit, and fail when market microstructure changes or when many firms crowd the same signal. Credit and private equity models inherit biased or incomplete data, and explainability is limited when deep networks are used. Agent workflows are promising but brittle, with error propagation, tool misuse, and unclear accountability. Governance is unsettled: regulators and courts are still defining how fiduciary duty, disclosure, and liability apply when AI informs investment decisions.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants the economic backdrop starts with Macroeconomic Econometrics, which covers growth, inflation, and nowcasting models. For trading and market reading, Quantitative Trading and Reading the Market's Language pair signal discovery with text based sentiment and topic extraction. Private Equity and Deal Sourcing and Fixed Income and Credit Risk show how AI is used in private company screening, merger and acquisition analysis, borrower scoring, and covenant monitoring, with the site's 357 merger and acquisition filings as a concrete base. Portfolio Construction and Alternative Data connect asset allocation to the non traditional inputs that feed it, from satellite imagery to transaction records. Agent Workflows in Finance explains how models are chained for research and operations, while Crypto Markets and Decentralised Finance covers the 24 hour programmatic venues. Governance and Fiduciary Risk sits above all of them and links to the site's 222 compliance and regulation pages, where duties, disclosures, and liability are mapped.
